commandWords.means: Translate the English sentence into Spanish.
commandWords.doThis: Translate meaning, not word for word; check tense, gender agreement and accents before moving on.

commandWords.means: Translate the Spanish sentence into English.
commandWords.doThis: Produce natural English; do not leave any Spanish word untranslated, and check tense carefully (preterite vs imperfect vs perfect).

commandWords.means: State a fact or piece of information briefly.
commandWords.doThis: Give a short, direct answer in the required language with no extra justification needed.

commandWords.means: Write about the given topic in an extended piece.
commandWords.doThis: Use a range of tenses, connectives and opinions; aim for the word count given and check verb endings match the subject.

commandWords.means: Describe what you see in the image during the speaking exam.
commandWords.doThis: Use present tense for what is happening, mention people, place, objects and a general observation or opinion.

commandWords.means: Respond to five prompts in an unscripted conversation with the teacher-examiner.
commandWords.doThis: Answer directly, use the correct tense implied by each prompt, and produce a spontaneous reply to the unpredictable question.

commandWords.means: Support your opinion with a reason, not just state it.
commandWords.doThis: Use porque, ya que or dado que followed by a specific reason, not a vague comment.

commandWords.means: Identify similarities and/or differences between two things.
commandWords.doThis: Use comparative structures (mas...que, menos...que, tan...como) to directly link the two items being compared.

sections.title: Verb tense formation (text tables): endings and key irregulars
sections.note: Regular endings shown for -AR/-ER/-IR patterns using hablar, comer, vivir as models; key irregulars given separately.

items.detail: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan (I speak, you speak, he/she speaks, we speak, you-all speak, they speak).
como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen (I eat, you eat, he/she eats, we eat, you-all eat, they eat).
vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, vivís, viven (I live, you live, he/she lives, we live, you-all live, they live).

ser: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son. estar: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están. tener: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen. ir: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van. hacer: hago, haces, hace, hacemos, hacéis, hacen.
hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron (I spoke, you spoke, he/she spoke, we spoke, you-all spoke, they spoke). Note accent on 1st/3rd person singular.
comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron / viví, viviste, vivió, vivimos, vivisteis, vivieron.

ser/ir (same form): fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. hacer: hice, hiciste, hizo, hicimos, hicisteis, hicieron. tener: tuve, tuviste, tuvo, tuvimos, tuvisteis, tuvieron. estar: estuve, estuviste, estuvo, estuvimos, estuvisteis, estuvieron.
hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban (I used to speak / was speaking, etc).
comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían / vivía, vivías, vivía, vivíamos, vivíais, vivían.
ser: era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran. ir: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban. ver: veía, veías, veía, veíamos, veíais, veían. (Only these three verbs are irregular in the imperfect.)
ir (present tense) + a + infinitive, e.g. voy a estudiar (I am going to study), vamos a comer (we are going to eat).

items.term: Simple future regular endings (all verb types)
items.detail: Add é, ás, á, emos, éis, án to the FULL infinitive: hablaré, hablarás, hablará, hablaremos, hablaréis, hablarán (I will speak, etc).
tener->tendr-, hacer->har-, poder->podr-, decir->dir-, salir->saldr-, poner->pondr-, venir->vendr-; then add the normal future endings, e.g. tendré (I will have).
Add ía, ías, ía, íamos, íais, ían to the FULL infinitive: hablaría, hablarías, hablaría, hablaríamos, hablaríais, hablarían (I would speak, etc).
Same irregular stems as the future: tendr-, har-, podr-, dir-, saldr-, pondr-, vendr-, then add conditional endings, e.g. tendría (I would have).
Present tense of haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) + past participle, e.g. he comido (I have eaten), ha hablado (he/she has spoken).
-AR verbs: stem + ado (hablado). -ER/-IR verbs: stem + ido (comido, vivido).
hacer->hecho, decir->dicho, escribir->escrito, ver->visto, poner->puesto, volver->vuelto, romper->roto, abrir->abierto, morir->muerto.
Take the yo form of the present tense, remove the -o, then add opposite endings: -AR verbs use e, es, e, emos, éis, en; -ER/-IR verbs use a, as, a, amos, áis, an. E.g. hablar->hable; comer->coma.
ser->sea, estar->esté, ir->vaya, haber->haya, saber->sepa, dar->dé - these do not follow the yo-form pattern and must be learned separately.

items.term: Radical-changing verbs in the present tense
items.detail: e->ie (querer: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren); o->ue (poder: puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden); e->i (pedir: pido, pides, pide, pedimos, pedís, piden). All persons change except nosotros/vosotros.
Used for identity, characteristics, origin, profession, time and dates, e.g. Soy español, Es profesora.
Used for location, temporary states and feelings, and with the gerund for continuous actions, e.g. Estoy cansado, Está en Madrid, Estoy comiendo.
Also used in fixed expressions: tener hambre (to be hungry), tener sed (to be thirsty), tener... años (to be... years old), tener que + infinitive (to have to).
Used for weather (hace sol, hace frío) and time expressions (hace dos años = two years ago).
Used alone (voy al colegio) and to form the near future (voy a + infinitive).
Radical-changing (o->ue); followed directly by an infinitive, e.g. puedo ayudar (I can help).
Radical-changing (e->ie); followed by an infinitive or noun, e.g. quiero viajar (I want to travel).
Used with an indirect object pronoun: me gusta (I like, singular thing), me gustan (I like, plural things), me gustaría (I would like).
Only used to form compound tenses (he comido = I have eaten); never used alone to mean 'to possess' (use tener for that).
Irregular yo form (digo); irregular preterite (dije, dijiste, dijo...) and irregular future stem (dir-).
Irregular yo form (sé); use for facts and skills, e.g. Sé nadar (I know how to swim).
Irregular yo form (conozco); used for familiarity with people or places, e.g. Conozco a María.
Irregular yo form (pongo); irregular future/conditional stem (pondr-).
Irregular yo form (salgo); irregular future/conditional stem (saldr-).
Radical-changing (e->ie) plus irregular yo form (vengo); irregular future/conditional stem (vendr-).

sections.title: Opinion, justification, connectives and time markers

items.term: En mi opinión / A mi parecer / Desde mi punto de vista
items.detail: In my opinion / As I see it / From my point of view - higher-level openers for opinion sentences.

items.term: Creo que / Pienso que / Opino que
items.detail: I believe that / I think that / I am of the opinion that - followed by an indicative verb (not subjunctive) when stating a belief.
It seems to me that... - used to introduce a personal judgement about a topic.

items.term: porque / ya que / dado que / puesto que
items.detail: because / since / given that / since - all introduce a reason; ya que, dado que and puesto que are higher-level alternatives to porque.
however / nevertheless - used to introduce a contrasting point.
on the other hand / on the other hand (in contrast) - used to present an alternative viewpoint.
although - can be followed by indicative (known fact) or subjunctive (hypothetical/uncertain), e.g. aunque llueve (although it is raining) vs aunque llueva (although it may rain).
therefore / so - used to introduce a consequence or conclusion.
furthermore, in addition / also - used to add a further point.
first, then, afterwards, finally - sequencing connectives for narrating a series of events.

items.term: ayer, anoche, la semana pasada, el año pasado
items.detail: yesterday, last night, last week, last year - preterite time markers signalling a completed past action.

items.term: normalmente, todos los días, a menudo, de vez en cuando
items.detail: normally, every day, often, from time to time - present tense / imperfect habitual time markers.

items.term: mañana, la semana que viene, el año que viene, en el futuro
items.detail: tomorrow, next week, next year, in the future - near future / simple future time markers.
suddenly (preterite trigger, interrupting action), while (imperfect trigger, background action) - classic preterite/imperfect combination marker.
What, e.g. ¿Qué haces? (What are you doing?). Always carries an accent as a question word.
Who (singular/plural), e.g. ¿Quién es? (Who is it?).
When, e.g. ¿Cuándo naciste? (When were you born?).
Where / to where, e.g. ¿Dónde vives? (Where do you live?), ¿Adónde vas? (Where are you going to?).
Why (two words, with accent) - answered using porque (one word, no accent on final e), meaning because.
How, e.g. ¿Cómo es tu casa? (What is your house like?).
How much/how many, agrees with the noun, e.g. ¿Cuántos hermanos tienes? (How many siblings do you have?).
Which (one/ones), e.g. ¿Cuál prefieres? (Which do you prefer?).
cuando + present subjunctive when referring to a future event, e.g. Cuando termine mis estudios... (When I finish my studies...).
para que + subjunctive expresses purpose ('so that'), e.g. Estudio para que mis padres estén orgullosos (I study so that my parents are proud).
Impersonal expressions of necessity or importance take the subjunctive, e.g. Es importante que reciclemos (It is important that we recycle).
ojalá + subjunctive expresses a wish, e.g. Ojalá tenga éxito (I hope I am successful/If only I have success).
Si + present indicative, + present or future, e.g. Si tengo tiempo, voy al gimnasio (If I have time, I go to the gym).
Si + imperfect subjunctive, + conditional, e.g. Si tuviera dinero, viajaría más (If I had money, I would travel more).
más...que (more than), menos...que (less than), tan...como (as...as), e.g. Mi hermano es más alto que yo.
el/la/los/las + (noun) + más/menos + adjective, e.g. la ciudad más bonita de España (the prettiest city in Spain).
se + third person verb expresses a general/passive action without naming who does it, e.g. Se habla español (Spanish is spoken), Se reciclan las botellas.

items.term: Impersonal expressions: hay que / se debe / es necesario
items.detail: hay que + infinitive (one must), se debe + infinitive (one should), es necesario + infinitive (it is necessary to) - all express obligation without a named subject.

items.term: Using a range of tenses in one paragraph
items.detail: Combining preterite, imperfect and future/conditional in a single answer (e.g. narrating past, describing background, then stating future plans) is explicitly rewarded at higher tier.

items.term: Using a negative structure beyond no
items.detail: nunca (never), nadie (nobody), nada (nothing), tampoco (neither) placed before the verb or with no...before and the negative word after, e.g. No como nunca carne.

sections.title: Topic vocabulary banks
sections.note: Matches the topics covered in the main file: customs and traditions, work/study, and the global dimension.

items.term: la fiesta / el festival / la celebración
items.detail: the party/festival / the festival / the celebration - core customs and traditions vocabulary.

items.term: la Navidad / la Semana Santa / el Día de los Muertos
items.detail: Christmas / Holy Week (Easter) / Day of the Dead - named festivals in Spain and Latin America.

items.term: los reyes magos / los fuegos artificiales / el desfile
items.detail: the Three Kings / fireworks / the parade - festival vocabulary.

items.term: el trabajo / el puesto / la entrevista / el currículum
items.detail: the job / the position / the interview / the CV - work and careers vocabulary.

items.term: el aprendizaje / la formación profesional / la carrera universitaria
items.detail: the apprenticeship / vocational training / the university degree - post-16 study vocabulary.

items.term: ganar un sueldo / estar en paro / jubilarse
items.detail: to earn a salary / to be unemployed / to retire - work-related verb phrases.

items.term: la contaminación / el calentamiento global / la sequía
items.detail: pollution / global warming / drought - environmental problems vocabulary (global dimension).

items.term: la deforestación / la especie en peligro de extinción / reciclar
items.detail: deforestation / endangered species / to recycle - environment and conservation vocabulary.

items.term: la pobreza / el hambre / la falta de vivienda
items.detail: poverty / hunger / homelessness - social issues vocabulary (global dimension).

items.term: el voluntariado / la ONG / recaudar fondos
items.detail: volunteering / the NGO (non-governmental organisation) / to raise funds - charity and volunteering vocabulary.

items.term: la igualdad / los derechos humanos / la discriminación
items.detail: equality / human rights / discrimination - social issues vocabulary.

items.term: el medio ambiente / sostenible / las energías renovables
items.detail: the environment / sustainable / renewable energies - environment vocabulary linking to global issues.

sections.title: Exam structure: all four papers with timings, and speaking openers

items.detail: Three parts in one recorded assessment: role-play (based on a photo/situation), photo card discussion, and general conversation on two themes; total 7-9 minutes plus 12 minutes supervised preparation time, worth 25% of the GCSE.

Five prompts/tasks (including one unprepared question) based on a short scenario card; respond in Spanish to each bullet point in turn, using the correct tense (often present or a past tense) as implied by the prompt.
Describe a photo and answer follow-up questions linked to the theme; discussion lasts about 3-4 minutes at Higher tier.
Discussion of two themes chosen from the specification (one may be the same as the photo card theme), lasting about 5-6 minutes at Higher tier, requiring a range of tenses and opinions.
Quisiera... (I would like...), ¿Puedo...? (Can I...?), Prefiero... (I prefer...), ¿Cuesta...? (Does it cost...?), Me gustaría reservar/comprar... (I would like to book/buy...).

En la foto se ve/hay... (In the photo you can see/there is...), En primer plano... (In the foreground...), Al fondo... (In the background...), Me parece que... (It seems to me that...), Esto me recuerda a... (This reminds me of...).
Normalmente... (Normally...), El año pasado... (Last year...), En el futuro me gustaría... (In the future I would like to...), Por un lado... por otro lado... (On one hand... on the other hand...).
1 hour, worth 25% of the GCSE. Higher tier questions in Spanish and English, including some dictation-style and multiple-choice tasks; play the recording twice.

items.term: Paper 3: Reading and translation into English
items.detail: 1 hour, worth 25% of the GCSE. Includes a range of authentic and adapted texts plus a translation of a short passage from Spanish into English.

items.term: Paper 4: Writing including translation into Spanish
items.detail: 1 hour 20 minutes, worth 25% of the GCSE. Includes shorter and extended writing tasks (Higher tier extended answer around 130-150 words using at least two tenses and opinions) plus a translation of English sentences/passage into Spanish.
En mi opinión... (In my opinion...), Además... (Furthermore...), Sin embargo... (However...), Para concluir... (To conclude...), Si pudiera... (If I could...).

7-9 minutes plus 12 minutes supervised preparation, in a school-arranged window (12 April to 21 May 2027). Worth 25%. Prepare general conversation themes in advance but expect one unpredictable role-play question; speak clearly and correct yourself calmly if you make an error.
1 hour, worth 25%. Read every question before each recording starts, note numbers and negatives on first listen, and use the second playing to check and fill gaps.

1 hour, worth 25%. Skim all questions first, use cognates and context to guess unfamiliar words, and leave the English translation passage until confident of the rest of the paper since it is time-consuming to check.

1 hour 20 minutes, worth 25%. Plan the extended writing answer for tense variety and opinions before writing, complete the translation into Spanish last if it is worth fewer marks, and leave 5 minutes to check verb endings and accents.

items.term: General accent-checking rule for all written papers
items.detail: Read back every verb ending and check accents on words like está vs esta, sí vs si, and preterite endings (-ó vs -o) since these change meaning or tense.

items.term: Equipment and setup for the speaking exam
items.detail: Bring the role-play and photo card stimulus cards you are given in preparation time, plus any notes made in the 12 minutes; no dictionaries are allowed in the preparation room.
Mentally rehearse opinion phrases and at least one sentence in the past, present and future tense so a range of tenses comes out naturally in the general conversation.

items.term: Final check before submitting Paper 4 writing
items.detail: Reread the extended writing task for tense variety (at least two tenses), adjective agreement, and that the word count target of 130 to 150 words has been met.

topics.name: Theme 1 Identity and Culture: Customs and Traditions
subtopics: Festivals and celebrations in Spain and Latin America
Food, meals and regional specialities
Family celebrations and religious traditions
Describing a past celebration using the preterite and imperfect together
Expressing opinions with justification using porque, ya que and dado que
Comparatives and superlatives
Higher-tier vocabulary for cultural comparison
Photo-card description for the speaking exam

cards.front: When do you use the preterite rather than the imperfect in Spanish?
cards.back: The preterite describes completed single actions in the past; the imperfect describes ongoing, repeated or background situations.

cards.front: Give the first person preterite of celebrar.
cards.back: Celebré - I celebrated. Note the written accent on the final e; without it, celebre is the subjunctive.

cards.front: How do you say in my opinion in Spanish, at higher level?
cards.back: En mi opinión, or a mi parecer, or desde mi punto de vista.

cards.front: How do you form the superlative in Spanish?
cards.back: Definite article plus más or menos plus adjective, e.g. la fiesta más importante.

cards.front: Give three linking words that raise your writing grade.
cards.back: Sin embargo (however), aunque (although), por lo tanto (therefore), ya que (since).

cloze: The Spanish {{c1::preterite}} tense describes completed actions in the past.
The Spanish {{c1::imperfect}} tense describes what used to happen or was happening.

topics.name: Theme 4 Future Aspirations, Study and Work
subtopics: Jobs, professions and workplace vocabulary
Applying for work, CVs, interviews and work experience
Post-16 study choices, university and apprenticeships
Future plans using the near future and the simple future tense
The conditional tense to describe what you would like to do
Using the subjunctive after cuando and para que at higher level
Advantages and disadvantages of different careers
Role-play conventions for the speaking exam

cards.front: How do you form the near future tense in Spanish?
cards.back: Ir conjugated plus a plus the infinitive, e.g. voy a estudiar - I am going to study.

cards.front: How do you form the simple future of regular verbs?
cards.back: Add é, ás, á, emos, éis, án to the infinitive, e.g. estudiaré - I will study.

cards.front: How do you form the conditional?
cards.back: Add ía, ías, ía, íamos, íais, ían to the infinitive, e.g. me gustaría - I would like.

cards.front: Which mood follows cuando when talking about the future?
cards.back: The present subjunctive, e.g. cuando termine mis estudios - when I finish my studies.

cards.front: Translate: I would like to work abroad because I want to improve my Spanish.
cards.back: Me gustaría trabajar en el extranjero porque quiero mejorar mi español.

cloze: The near future is formed with {{c1::ir}} plus {{c2::a}} plus the infinitive.
Me gustaría means {{c1::I would like}} and uses the {{c2::conditional}} tense.
After cuando referring to the future, Spanish uses the {{c1::subjunctive}}.

topics.name: Theme 5 International and Global Dimension
subtopics: Environmental problems and solutions
Global events, sport and campaigns
Social issues: poverty, homelessness, volunteering
Debería and hay que for obligation and recommendation
The passive and impersonal se constructions
Se debe, se puede and es necesario que structures
Extended written response of 130 to 150 words with two tenses and opinions
Translation into and out of Spanish

cards.front: How do you say we should recycle more in Spanish?
cards.back: Deberíamos reciclar más.

cards.front: What does hay que plus infinitive express?
cards.back: An impersonal obligation - one must, it is necessary to.

cards.front: Give three environmental problems in Spanish.
cards.back: La contaminación (pollution), el calentamiento global (global warming), la deforestación (deforestation), la sequía (drought).

cards.front: What is the impersonal se used for?
cards.back: To say something is done in general without naming who does it, e.g. se recicla el plástico - plastic is recycled.

cards.front: How many words should a higher-tier extended writing answer be?
cards.back: Around 130 to 150 words, using at least two tenses and developed opinions.

cloze: {{c1::Hay que}} plus an infinitive expresses an impersonal obligation.
La {{c1::contaminación}} means pollution and el {{c2::calentamiento global}} means global warming.
The higher-tier extended writing task requires about {{c1::130 to 150}} words.

topics.name: Grammar Core and Exam Technique
subtopics: Present tense: regular, radical-changing and irregular verbs
Ser versus estar
Preterite, imperfect, perfect, pluperfect, future and conditional
Present and imperfect subjunctive triggers
Direct and indirect object pronouns and their position
Reflexive verbs and reflexive pronouns
Adjective agreement and position
Por versus para
Listening exam strategy: reading questions first, catching numbers and negatives
Reading exam strategy: cognates, false friends and question order
Speaking exam: role play, photo card, general conversation timings
Writing exam: structure, tense variety, checking agreement and accents

cards.front: Explain the difference between ser and estar.
cards.back: Ser is for permanent or defining characteristics, origin, profession and time. Estar is for temporary states, moods and location.

cards.front: When do you use por and when para?
cards.back: Por for cause, exchange, duration and movement through. Para for purpose, destination, deadline and recipient.

cards.front: Where do object pronouns usually go in Spanish?
cards.back: Before the conjugated verb, or attached to the end of an infinitive, gerund or positive command.

cards.front: Name three tenses that will lift a higher-tier written answer.
cards.back: The preterite, the conditional and the subjunctive, alongside the present and near future.

cards.front: Give a fast listening exam strategy.
cards.back: Read the questions before the recording, predict likely vocabulary, and listen actively for numbers, negatives and time markers on the first play.

cards.front: Which five words change meaning only because of a written accent?
cards.back: sí (yes) versus si (if), él (he) versus el (the), tú (you) versus tu (your), más (more) versus mas (but), sólo/solo and qué (what, in questions) versus que (that).

cloze: {{c1::Ser}} is used for permanent characteristics and {{c2::estar}} for temporary states and location.
{{c1::Por}} expresses cause or duration, while {{c2::para}} expresses purpose or destination.
Object pronouns go {{c1::before}} the conjugated verb in Spanish.
The word {{c1::sí}} with an accent means yes, while si without an accent means if.
